headline: California auto severity pushes Kemper to a narrow loss
summary_short: Kemper posted a Q1 FY2026 net loss of $1.7 million (diluted EPS -$0.03) versus $99.7 million net income a year earlier, as the Specialty P&C combined ratio deteriorated to 106.7% from 92.7% on higher California bodily-injury and property-damage severity.
summary_long: Adjusted Consolidated Net Operating Income fell to $12.5 million from $106.4 million, driven by a 13.1-point deterioration in Specialty Personal Automobile's underlying loss ratio from higher California bodily-injury and property-damage severity and frequency, lower volumes, and a $28.0 million Florida Statutory Profit Limit Refund, partly offset by a 4.7% rate-driven rise in earned premium per exposure. Net investment income rose 5.8% to $107.1 million on higher alternative-investment earnings and fixed-maturity yields. Operating cash flow fell to $88.8 million from $180.0 million on lower personal-auto volumes. The company paid a $0.32/share dividend and repurchased no stock this quarter ($304.2 million remains authorized). No forward guidance was issued.

drivers.explanation: Net income fell $101.4M y/y "due primarily to lower Adjusted Consolidated Net Operating Income," itself down $93.9M on Specialty Personal Automobile underwriting deterioration.

Decline was "primarily driven by lower earned premiums," down $88.6M on lower personal-auto volumes, a $28.0M Florida profit-limit refund, and Non-Core run-off, partly offset by commercial-auto growth.

Attributed to a deterioration in Specialty Personal Automobile's underlying loss ratio from higher California claim severity and frequency, lower volumes, and the Florida refund, partly offset by higher earned premium per exposure.

Tracks the net income swing to a loss; diluted share count also fell to 58.7M from 64.7M a year earlier via buybacks completed in prior quarters, which would have partly cushioned EPS had income been positive.

Underlying losses and LAE rose to 84.0% of earned premiums (+13.1pts) "due to higher claim severity and frequency" in California bodily injury and property damage, partly offset by a 4.7% rate-driven increase in earned premium per exposure.
Increase was "mostly driven by increased earnings on alternative investments" and higher fixed-maturity and mortgage-loan levels, partly offset by lower average short-term invested assets.
Decline was "primarily driven by lower personal automobile volumes," partly offset by higher average earned premiums per exposure from rate increases.
Not separately explained in the release beyond the quarter's net loss and other comprehensive loss; q/q figures are the only reliably matched pair on this filing's balance sheet.
Not explained in the release; the y/y change is immaterial (+0.2%) and no debt issuance or repayment is disclosed for the quarter.
